guide.title: Spine & Spinal Motion Restriction
guide.lead: Restrict spinal movement for the patients who need it, not everyone in a crash. Use clear criteria, then a collar and a scoop or vacuum mattress. Long backboards are for getting people out, not for the ride. Watch the breathing and BP in high cord injuries.

sections.title: Blunt trauma: who needs SMR?
exclude: None of the above (NEXUS-negative): no SMR needed
Penetrating trauma without neuro deficit: no SMR (it delays care)

steps.title: Manual in-line stabilisation
steps.text: Head neutral, unless that causes pain or resistance.

steps.title: Collar
steps.text: Size from the angle of the jaw to the top of the shoulder.

steps.title: Move as a unit
steps.text: Scoop stretcher or minimal log roll.

steps.title: Transport
steps.text: Vacuum mattress or stretcher with head blocks; take the long board out as soon as practical.

sections.title: Cord injuries
rows: Injury around C3–C5: breathing may fail; above C3: apnea
Low BP, slow pulse, warm dry skin
Neurogenic shock: fluids, vasopressors, atropine (ALS); avoid systolic below 90 mmHg

quiz.q: Low-speed rear-end crash: GCS 15, no neck pain or tenderness, no neuro signs, no distracting injury, sober. SMR?
options: Collar and backboard for every crash

quiz.q: Ejected, GCS 6, rebar through the chest, BP 76/50, SpO₂ 88%. Priority?
options: Penetrating chest trauma in shock: stabilise the rebar, oxygen, airway support, emergency transport; SMR only without delaying care
quiz.explanation: Don't let SMR delay life-saving care.

quiz.q: Alert after a crash: neck pain, tingling hands, BP 86/52, pulse 56, warm dry skin. Cause of the low BP?
options: Neurogenic shock from a cervical cord injury
No midline tenderness, not intoxicated, alert, no neuro deficit, no distracting injury

quiz.q: Long backboards today are mainly for:

options: Angle of the jaw to the top of the shoulder
quiz.explanation: Too big flexes, too small extends.

quiz.q: Stab wound to the neck, no neuro deficit. SMR?
options: No: it delays care and doesn't help

quiz.q: A diver can't move arms or legs and breathes with the belly only. Level?
Arms weaker than legs after a neck hyperextension injury:
quiz.explanation: Common in older adults after falls.

quiz.q: Minimum systolic BP to avoid in spinal cord injury:

flashcards.question: NEXUS criteria
flashcards.answer: Cleared only if all negative: midline tenderness, intoxication, altered alertness, focal neuro deficit, distracting injury.

flashcards.question: Spinal vs neurogenic shock
flashcards.answer: Spinal shock: temporary loss of all cord function below the injury. Neurogenic shock: hypotension, bradycardia, warm dry skin from lost sympathetic tone.

flashcards.question: Neurogenic vs hypovolemic shock
flashcards.answer: Neurogenic: bradycardia, warm dry skin. Hypovolemic: tachycardia, cool pale clammy skin.

flashcards.question: Incomplete cord syndromes
flashcards.answer: Central: arms weaker than legs. Anterior: motor and pain loss, position sense kept. Brown-Séquard: same-side motor loss, opposite-side pain loss.

flashcards.question: Problems with long backboards
flashcards.answer: Pain, pressure injuries, restricted breathing, anxiety. Use them for extrication, not transport.

flashcards.question: SMR in penetrating trauma
flashcards.answer: Not recommended without a neuro deficit: it delays care and increases mortality.

flashcards.question: Moving a patient with SMR
flashcards.answer: In-line stabilisation; scoop stretcher or minimal log roll as a unit; vacuum mattress or stretcher with head blocks.

flashcards.question: Collar sizing
flashcards.answer: Angle of the jaw to the top of the shoulder (trapezius); head neutral.

critical.scenario: A belted driver hit a guardrail at about 70 km/h. Alert, no neck or back pain, no midline tenderness, normal neuro exam, sober, a minor forehead cut. He asks if he really needs a board.
critical.question: How do you apply current guidance?

options.t: He's NEXUS-negative: no SMR needed; document the assessment and still transport for evaluation
Everyone at highway speed gets a board

options.f: Airbag and frontal impact still warrant assessment.

options.t: Collar and board to be safe

critical.explanation: A minor forehead cut isn't a distracting injury.
critical.kpi: Applies selective spinal motion restriction criteria

critical.scenario: A man dived into shallow water: can't move arms or legs, no sensation below the shoulders, belly breathing. BP 84/58, pulse 52, SpO₂ 92%, warm dry skin.
critical.question: Level and priorities?

options.t: High cervical cord injury with neurogenic shock: in-line stabilisation and collar, scoop or vacuum mattress, support breathing (BVM if failing), fluids and ALS for vasopressors/atropine, keep warm

options.f: Arm involvement and belly breathing mean high cervical.

critical.explanation: The diaphragm (C3–C5) is all that's working: watch him closely.
critical.kpi: Recognizes high cervical cord injury with respiratory and neurogenic shock risk

critical.scenario: Frontal crash: alert, neck pain with midline tenderness at C5–C6, no neuro signs, and an obviously broken ankle.
critical.question: SMR approach?

options.t: SMR (midline tenderness and a distracting injury): sized collar, scoop stretcher and vacuum mattress or stretcher with head blocks; splint the ankle
Wait for the ankle pain to settle, then recheck the neck

options.f: Use a scoop or vacuum mattress.

critical.kpi: Applies SMR for midline tenderness and distracting injury
